trigger_condition: `--as <role>` is accepted with no reason whenever the claimed role owns the gate, so one session can write `ticket` as dev then `review` and `done` as qa; `guard_self_approval` compares the builder with the claimed actor, not with the session.
guard_snippet: Require `--reason` for any explicit `--as`, log `by qa (as=explicit, reason: ...)`, or drop `--as` and require the `role` verb to persist a handoff.
potential_consequence: Separation of duties is self-attested: a single agent builds, reviews, and approves a ticket, and `validate` certifies it.

trigger_condition: A `done` return with no `role` or `action` is accepted when `--expect-role` and `--expect-action` are omitted; the ownership check is skipped entirely.
guard_snippet: For `status == done`, reject a return that does not name both fields unless `--allow-unattributed --reason` is supplied, and log the waiver.
potential_consequence: The only runtime proof that the right role produced the action can be dropped by a command-line omission.

trigger_condition: A returned artifact is accepted if it exists, is non-empty, and is inside the root; the computed `changed` set is never consulted, so any pre-existing file passes.
guard_snippet: When git status is available, require at least one claimed artifact to appear in `touched_paths`, or add `--allow-unchanged-artifact --reason`.
potential_consequence: A handoff that produced nothing is accepted, and the gate passes on paper.

trigger_condition: A decided gate with no `actor` passes `validate`; `guard_self_approval` then skips the check because the builder is unknown.
guard_snippet: In `cmd_validate`, fail every passed/overridden/skipped gate missing `actor` (or backfill `actor: null` in `migrate` so the gap is visible).
potential_consequence: Deleting one YAML line disables the self-approval audit permanently, with a green suite and a clean validate.

trigger_condition: The one documented `init` command always passes `--model <model>`; on an existing ledger whose model is confirmed, a silent detector yields `unknown` and `init` refuses as a downgrade.
guard_snippet: Split the snippet: `--model` only when creating; omit it when appending, and change the model with `set --path bmad.model`.
potential_consequence: Adding a workstream pushes the agent toward `--force --reason`, the destructive reset, or off the documented path.

trigger_condition: `init` appends a workstream after detection changes the model while any other workstream is paused or done; the model-migration loop fails before the append.
guard_snippet: Do not run the document-wide model migration on the append path: keep the recorded model when `existing`, or scope the migration to active workstreams.
potential_consequence: The documented add-a-workstream operation is unavailable exactly after a BMAD upgrade, with an error that names neither the requested action nor the fix.

trigger_condition: `done` rewrites every pending/active phase to `done` in one write, with no per-phase actor or reason, though the gate matrix says a phase advance by a foreign role needs both.
guard_snippet: Record each auto-advanced phase in the close note and audit line, or require `phases[].complete` plus an explicit per-phase `set ... status done` first.
potential_consequence: Plan and Build can be advanced by the closer with no recorded decision, at the one moment the rule matters.

trigger_condition: `reconcile --write` blocks an open gate when its artifact is missing; once the artifact appears, `set ... passed` is refused and no documented command clears the block.
guard_snippet: Document the clear path (`set ... --value open`, then decide) or have `reconcile --write` return a blocked gate to `open` when its pointer now resolves.
potential_consequence: Agents take the visible escape (override with a reason) or hand-edit, polluting the close summary with overrides that are really recovered state.

trigger_condition: Headless `status: ready` never says whether to run the next action: "legal to run" reads as execute, while "stop at the next gate" reads as stop now.
guard_snippet: State: `ready` means run this one action now, then stop before `next_action.gate` and emit the block; it never authorizes a gate decision.
potential_consequence: Two headless consumers behave oppositely on the same ledger: one idles, one performs unrequested work.

trigger_condition: A ledger that `validate` and `migrate` cannot repair has no headless status; the only documented recovery, `init --force --reason`, is forbidden headless.
guard_snippet: Add a `ledger.corrupt` blocked row with the pointer, and state that only a human may reset it.
potential_consequence: An unattended run fabricates a status or improvises a reset, destroying the delivery history.

trigger_condition: `trivial` is defined as "reviewer can self-check", but the script refuses a review or done decision by the same role, with no size exemption.
guard_snippet: Change the sizing row to "reviewable in one pass by an independent role", or exempt `trivial` explicitly and document it in `validate`.
potential_consequence: The smallest track stalls at `build.review` for want of a second role, and the natural workaround is the `--as`/override hole.

trigger_condition: `menu.md` says `summary.actions[]` carries every `role_free` action including `advisory.*`, but the action catalog never includes the five advisory ids.
guard_snippet: Add an `ADVISORY_ACTION_IDS` list to `action_catalog`, or delete the promise and route advisory offers through `phase-map.md` only.
potential_consequence: A menu filtered as instructed cannot surface advisory actions, so `include_advisory_skills` has no runtime effect.

trigger_condition: Two statuses mean "the human declined this gate": §Gate interaction says a required gate is `overridden` and `skipped` is only for optional gates, while §Override rules and the `skip` verb require a reasoned `skipped` on required/conditional gates.
guard_snippet: Pick one status per level and make `validate` reject the other; make the `skip` verb write `overridden` for required/conditional gates.
potential_consequence: Ledgers become non-comparable and the close summary's override count depends on which file the agent read.

trigger_condition: Literal bash examples omit the required `--plan` (`set --workstream ...`, `ticket --id ...`), so copying them fails with a usage error.
guard_snippet: State once that examples elide the required `--plan`, and add `--plan {workflow.ledger_path}` to every literal command.
potential_consequence: Guardrail commands fail with usage errors and agents improvise hand edits or `--force`.

trigger_condition: Step 6 says a status-only request with no ledger is reported and offered, but steps 7-8 still run `reconcile` and `summary` against the missing file.
guard_snippet: Guard steps 7-10 on the ledger existing (or step 6 creating it); otherwise emit the short no-ledger status and stop.
potential_consequence: The most common first question in a new repo ends in two JSON `ledger not found` errors.

trigger_condition: Without `ruamel.yaml`, `_yaml()` raises on a null `YAML` and the script reports "cannot parse ledger", not a missing-dependency hint; the hand-edit fallback then forbids presenting a gate that no tool can validate.
guard_snippet: Fail fast with "ruamel.yaml is not installed; run with `uv run --no-cache <script>`", and give the fallback a stated validation bar.
potential_consequence: A healthy ledger is diagnosed as corrupt, or a hand-edited gate is presented unchecked.

trigger_condition: `init --force` always writes the fixed name `plan.yaml.bak`; a retry overwrites the only backup with the already-reset ledger.
guard_snippet: Refuse when the backup exists, rotate to a timestamped name, and document the restore path.
potential_consequence: The safety net presented for the destructive reset is destroyed on the second attempt.

trigger_condition: The ledger is saved before the audit line is appended; `plan_locked` restores on an exception but not on SIGKILL or a harness timeout, and nothing cross-checks decided gates against audit lines.
guard_snippet: Write the audit intent first, or add a validation that every decided gate has a matching audit line.
potential_consequence: The append-only trail silently loses the line explaining a gate decision, and no command reports it.

trigger_condition: `verify-return` has no `--workstream`; ownership is resolved from the active workstream, so a return for any other workstream is checked against the wrong track (or none when paused).
guard_snippet: Add `--workstream` and resolve `track` from that record, and rewrite handoff-protocol:86 to name the real command.
potential_consequence: The ownership check silently uses the wrong track in multi-workstream ledgers, and following the protocol literally is a usage error.

trigger_condition: A return lists its own `--return-file` or a `.tmp/` scratch file as an artifact and evidence; only the ledger and memlog are excluded.
guard_snippet: Add the resolved return-file and the ledger's sibling `.tmp/` to the exclusion set.
potential_consequence: Acceptance certifies a handoff with no deliverable artifact.

trigger_condition: Same as R13-02: a `done` return without role/action is accepted when the expectation flags are omitted.
guard_snippet: Require both fields for `done`, with a reasoned escape hatch.
potential_consequence: Role-less, action-less success defeats the separation-of-duties check.

trigger_condition: Phase evidence is append-only and a replaced phase must keep every entry; if an appended evidence file is later deleted or renamed, `done` can never pass without `--accept-missing-evidence` or a hand edit.
guard_snippet:
Allow clearing phase evidence with `set --path phases.

.evidence --value '[]' --reason`, re-validating the remainder.
potential_consequence: A stale pointer permanently traps close in a documented-but-unreachable repair path.

trigger_condition: A whole-phase `--replace` can carry `evidence` entries that do not exist; the replacement path does not run the file/containment checks that `append` runs.
guard_snippet: Validate every incoming evidence string with `is_file()` and `_inside()` before assigning the node.
potential_consequence: The ledger passes the write, then `reconcile` blocks the phase and `done` fails; the bad entries cannot be removed.

trigger_condition: Appending evidence with a numeric value such as `7` JSON-parses to an int, skips the string-only existence check, and stores an integer.
guard_snippet: Require every evidence entry to be a non-empty string before appending.
potential_consequence: The ledger validates until close, then blocks on a path that cannot exist.

trigger_condition: `done --accept-missing-tickets` closes a non-audit workstream with no ticket, marks the empty build phase `done`, and leaves a ledger that `validate` immediately rejects.
guard_snippet: Do not mark `phases.build` done when the waiver is used with no ticket, and add the close-note line the schema advertises.
potential_consequence: The command reports success, the next activation reports corruption, and the only repair is the destructive reset.

trigger_condition: Reopening an earlier phase and adding a ticket while later phases stay `done` leaves `verify`/`close` done over an undecided build gate.
guard_snippet: Reopen later non-pending phases with the earlier one, or refuse a ticket add while a later phase is done.
potential_consequence: `validate` reports an invalid ledger after a sequence the commands each accepted.

trigger_condition: Same as R13-06: appending after a model change fails on a paused or done sibling workstream.
guard_snippet: Keep the recorded model on the append path; never fail an append on a closed sibling.
potential_consequence: The append either fails or silently rewrites `bmad.model`.

trigger_condition: `migrate` skips done and paused workstreams and still returns ok, so a corrupt ledger whose only workstreams are closed stays invalid.
guard_snippet: Return `ok: false` when `skipped_workstreams` is non-empty, or repair them under the same `--reason`.
potential_consequence: The agent believes corruption is repaired while `validate` keeps failing.

trigger_condition: An unknown gate in the ledger is counted as blocking by `summary`, but `set` refuses its id and `migrate` does not drop it.
guard_snippet: Have `migrate` drop gates not in `GATE_NAMES` as the validate warning promises, or accept the id in `set`.
potential_consequence: The phase can never complete and `next_action` names an action that cannot be recorded.

trigger_condition: Pausing the active workstream clears `active_workstream` without updating the workstream's `updated`; `summary` then reports the most recently created sibling's track, size, phase, and role.
guard_snippet: Stamp `workstream['updated']` whenever a workstream becomes active or paused.
potential_consequence: Headless output and `current_role` describe a different workstream than the one just paused.

trigger_condition: `done` requires every artifact pointer to resolve, including pointers for optional gates that were never decided; a deleted optional artifact blocks close.
guard_snippet: Require pointers only for artifacts whose gate is required/conditional and decided.
potential_consequence: `summary` recommends close while `done` refuses on a stale optional pointer.

trigger_condition: `init --force` on a path that does not exist skips the `--reason` check because the guard sits inside the `exists()` branch.
guard_snippet: Check `--force` requires `--reason` before the existence branch.
potential_consequence: The destructive verb's reason requirement depends on whether a file happens to exist.

trigger_condition: `resize` with neither `--track` nor `--size` is a no-op except that it always pops `role_override`, changing `current_role`.
guard_snippet: Fail when neither flag is supplied; pop `role_override` only when a value changes.
potential_consequence: A typo silently changes which role owns the next action.

trigger_condition: A malformed `_bmad/config.toml` is surfaced by `detect` and refused by `init`, but `done` and `reconcile` resolve default folders and proceed.
guard_snippet: Fail in `done`/`reconcile` when `_CONFIG_ERRORS` is non-empty, as `init` does.
potential_consequence: Evidence is bound against default folders, so close is mis-checked or wrongly blocked.

trigger_condition: Every test that passes `--accept-missing-tickets` creates at least one ticket first, so the no-ticket branch that writes the invalid ledger is never reached.
guard_snippet: Add a test: init fix/trivial, close with `--accept-missing-tickets`, then assert `validate` ok and the close note names the accepted gap.
potential_consequence: The invalid-ledger regression (R13-25) ships green.
evidence: Ran the CLI: done returned ok, validate returned `phases.build is done with no ticket built`; no test asserts the accepted-gap close note.

trigger_condition: No test supplies exactly one `--expect-*-sha`; an `or` regression that accepts a partial digest would stay green.
guard_snippet: Assert that a one-flag call yields `digest_check: not_run`, `ok: false`, and a reason naming the missing digest.
potential_consequence: One matching digest could accept a return while the unhashed file was edited.
evidence: All `--expect-*-sha` occurrences in both test files are paired; a one-flag probe returns not_run/ok:false but nothing asserts it.

trigger_condition: `--allow-empty-artifacts` is asserted only for `ok`, not for the decision line it is documented to log.
guard_snippet: Assert the audit trail gains `accepted an empty artifact list (reason: ...)`.
potential_consequence: Dropping the audit write leaves no record of the waiver and the suite still passes.
evidence: The string appears only at sdlc_plan.py:6128; the test asserts only `allowed['ok']`.

trigger_condition: No test asserts that a manual phase skip writes the reason into `phases.<phase>.note`; only init's auto-skip is covered.
guard_snippet: Assert `note` equals the `--reason` after `set phases.<phase>.status skipped --reason ...`.
potential_consequence: The documented reason exists only in the memlog if the assignment regresses.
evidence: Ran the CLI and read back the note; no test covers the manual path.

trigger_condition: `force-headless` stages no ledger (`files: []`), so its rubric items "does not delete, back up, or replace an existing ledger" and "no plan.yaml.bak" are vacuous.
guard_snippet: Stage a ledger and memlog, assert both are byte-identical after the run, and assert no `.bak` exists.
potential_consequence: A run that executes `init --force` still passes the case meant to forbid it.
evidence: Read files:[] and the staging code; `init --force` on a fresh root creates plan.yaml and no .bak, so all three assertions hold.

trigger_condition: The README says headless cases assert the block's key set and that two add a derived-status check; `fix-trivial-ready` and `status-empty` carry neither.
guard_snippet: Add the key-set omission rubric and the derived-status rubric to those cases, or correct the README to name the cases that have them.
potential_consequence: A ready block with the omitted keys passes, and `needs_input` can be echoed without derivation.
evidence: Parsed every rubric: 10 headless cases carry the key-set line; fix-trivial-ready, status-empty, force-headless, and consent-before-commit do not; `derived` appears only in the two role cases.

trigger_condition: Self-approval is tested only through the `ticket` command; the `set` route for `tickets.<id>.gates.review` has no foreign-role test.
guard_snippet: Mirror `test_self_approval_is_refused` using `set --path tickets.T1.gates.review.status`.
potential_consequence: Dropping the `set`-path guard lets DEV self-review, and `done` does not re-check actors.
consumer: the `set` ticket-gate editor used by the conductor
evidence: Ran the set command as DEV and got the refusal; the only test for the message uses `ticket`; the main suite injects `--as <owner>`.

trigger_condition: No test supplies a valid `[track_action_overrides]` entry; the shipped table is empty, so the advertised first-precedence rule is never exercised.
guard_snippet: Write a temp config with `fix.verify.trace = dev` and assert dev's `role_allowed` is true and qa's false.
potential_consequence: Removing the override lookup leaves the suite green, and customized installs silently flip ownership.
evidence: Tests touch the table only for invalid-key validation; a temp-config probe confirmed the override works today.

trigger_condition: Every role overlay promises to add judgment only, then restates base criteria; the overlays load with the base at activation, so the restatement buys nothing and creates eight drift surfaces.
guard_snippet: Merge each role's overlay into one ~290-word file containing only true deltas; delete restated gate rows, the six copies of the transition-pointer sentence, and dev/phase-map's verbatim ready-ticket sources.
potential_consequence: 1,100 words on the activation path and repeated opportunities for base and overlay to disagree.

trigger_condition: Four invariants are each stated three or four times in different words: phase advance needs a reason, override needs a reason, no self-approval, and summary wins on levels.
guard_snippet: Keep one canonical sentence per rule in its owning file and a bare pointer everywhere else.
potential_consequence: The restatements have already diverged in detail, so the rule depends on load order.

trigger_condition: SKILL.md restates the role action lists and the five-step role-resolution ladder that `role-config.toml` says not to duplicate in prose.
guard_snippet: Keep the orientation and the explicit-`--role` input rule in SKILL.md; move the ladder to the `role-config.toml` header the script implements.
potential_consequence: Two copies of ownership resolution drift, and the TOML is authoritative only in name.

trigger_condition: Headless and handoff point at each other in a cycle for the emitted block, and the headless trigger is stated four times.
guard_snippet: Move the role-mismatch example into `headless.md` §Emitted block and delete handoff-protocol §Headless JSON; make §References the sole trigger index.
potential_consequence: A headless-only read cannot close the loop between the two authority files.

trigger_condition: 170 words of mixed ownership, gate-id-vs-action-id, actor, and self-approval prose sit between the purpose line and the gate table.
guard_snippet: Lead with the table; move ownership to `role-config.toml` and the actor rule to `ledger-schema.md`.
potential_consequence: The artifact the agent came for is delayed, and one claim is repeated in §Override rules.

trigger_condition: The `Level` and `Condition` columns restate each other and re-encode the track-by-size logic that `summary` computes and `phase-map.md` §Sizing explains.
guard_snippet: Condense to one "When it applies" column and point at §Sizing for the derived level.
potential_consequence: A third copy of the same matrix can disagree with the authoritative one.

trigger_condition: Sixteen flat guardrail bullets put filesystem isolation and the eval prohibition at positions 14-16, competing with the least load-bearing rules.
guard_snippet: Group into Gate/role invariants, Safety/isolation, and Conduct; move "never present a gate from an unvalidated ledger" into the first group.
potential_consequence: The rules most likely to prevent a bad write lose salience.

trigger_condition: The first instruction uses workstream, track, size, phase, action, and gate before any file defines them; values live only in later-loaded references.
guard_snippet: Add a six-line vocabulary block under §Overview with each term and its values inline.
potential_consequence: Every activation pays several lookup hops before the first instruction is executable.

trigger_condition: Loop step 5 restates the handoff acceptance rule that handoff-protocol §Return contract owns, one step after that file was loaded.
guard_snippet: Keep the `verify-return` command and replace the prose with "Acceptance criteria: handoff-protocol §Return contract."
potential_consequence: Two copies of a six-bullet rule drift.

trigger_condition: "Reads only the ledger and artifacts" appears five times across handoff-protocol, and the validation checklist repeats the digest bullet.
guard_snippet: Merge lifecycle and what-the-conductor-keeps into one "What crosses the boundary" block; keep the blocked-gate worked example plus a pointer; drop checklist item 3.
potential_consequence: Redundant statements of the same boundary drift independently.

trigger_condition: The verb rows for skip, override, revise, done, and reopen restate gate status semantics already owned by gate-matrix.
guard_snippet: Condense to verb plus argument shape and point at §Override rules and §Reopening.
potential_consequence: A fourth copy of override/reopen/close rules can disagree.

trigger_condition: §Sizing's Path column and §Per-track flows are two notations for the same gate-skip logic; the coarse one can only disagree with the fine one.
guard_snippet: Keep the trivial short-circuit and the fix/audit exceptions in §Sizing; defer multi-step ordering to §Per-track flows.
potential_consequence: Readers get two answers for which gates apply.

trigger_condition: Seven hand-maintained Contents blocks duplicate headings and are the first thing to drift after a rename; SKILL.md, customize.toml, the template, and all eight overlays have none.
guard_snippet: Cut them, or apply one policy to every file.
potential_consequence: Stale navigation misdirects a maintainer; 162 words on the activation path.

trigger_condition: The same `detect` command, project-local warning, and no-silent-overwrite rule appear in two files loaded at different times.
guard_snippet: Let one side own the model rules and the other cite it.
potential_consequence: The two copies drift, and it is unclear which is authoritative.

trigger_condition: "`skipped` ... use it only for an optional gate or when the phase itself is being skipped" contradicts §Override rules, the `skip` verb, and ledger-schema, which all require reasoned `skipped` on required/conditional gates.
guard_snippet: Replace with: "`skipped` is its own status: an optional gate skips without a reason; skipping a required or conditional gate is an override and needs one."
potential_consequence: An executor refuses a legal skip or writes `overridden` when the user said skip.

trigger_condition: "no single role performs all three on the same ticket" has no three-item antecedent in SKILL.md.
guard_snippet: Say "builds, reviews, and approves the same ticket".
potential_consequence: The separation-of-duties rule is vague at the point a reader meets it first.

trigger_condition: "This table names each persona and what the role owns" uses `role` for persona two sentences before `role` means the conductor role.
guard_snippet: Use "what each owns" or "what the persona owns".
potential_consequence: Readers can take the persona table as PM/DEV/QA ownership.

trigger_condition: "The subagent gets this brief plus its `Role:` and `Action:` lines, and `--role ...`" has no clear owner for `its`; the template already contains those lines.
guard_snippet: Say "the brief, with its `Role:` and `Action:` lines filled in, plus ...".
potential_consequence: The flags read as parts of the brief rather than a separate command.

trigger_condition: "records the blocked gate with the `--reason` above" refers to a flag that does not appear above in that section.
guard_snippet: Say "using the message above as `--reason`".
potential_consequence: An executor hunts for a command that is not there.

trigger_condition: "Run `summary` with the step 7 flags" makes the reader leaf back two steps to another command's flag set.
guard_snippet: Name `--plan` and `--project-root` explicitly.
potential_consequence: The invocation cannot be copied without a lookup, and the flag sets may differ.

trigger_condition: "`ok: false` means `blocked`; judge scope and evidence" names no subject, so the phase, workstream, or returned status can be marked blocked.
guard_snippet: Say "means the return was rejected: treat the action as `blocked`".
potential_consequence: The scope of the block is misapplied.

trigger_condition: "No session summary passed — only ledger artifacts" drops a conjunction and reads as artifacts of the ledger.
guard_snippet: Say "only the ledger and artifact files".
potential_consequence: The rule appears to forbid exactly what it permits.

trigger_condition: "Overlays add role notes" is the lone variant of "role deltas" used at step 9 and in every overlay.
guard_snippet: Use "role deltas".
potential_consequence: A reader cannot tell whether notes and deltas are the same thing.

trigger_condition: "`gate-matrix.md` defines gate levels" sits beside "summary wins on gate levels", inviting the reading that the matrix overrides summary.
guard_snippet: Say "defines the gate table and level rules".
potential_consequence: The precedence rule is misread in the one place it is stated.

trigger_condition: "List every entry ... whose `phase` matches, whose `role` equals `current_role`, plus ..." is missing the conjunction and reads as an unrestrained second filter.
guard_snippet: Insert "and" before the second relative clause.
potential_consequence: A menu lists actions the role may not run.

trigger_condition: A headless run emits `status: blocked`, but the audit trail records only workstream creation and a `phases.<phase>.note updated` line; no line repeats the block, though the eval README says blocking cases assert it.
guard_snippet: Add a `log --type blocked --text "<action>: <reason>"` call to the activation block path, or relax the rubric to accept the note line as the record.
potential_consequence: The audit trail cannot explain why a run stopped; 6 of 17 graded cases failed the same expectation.

location: references/headless.md:3; SKILL.md:158-159; start-greenfield and scope-capture transcripts
trigger_condition: Two graded runs wrote `/tmp/summary.json` and read it back to assemble the block, while `headless.md` says scratch stays under `{project-root}` and never in the system temp directory.
guard_snippet: Name the scratch path in the activation steps and in §Emitted block, where the model builds the JSON, not only in the headless preamble.
potential_consequence: Isolation fails in the one mode that runs unattended, and the run leaves files it must not leave.

trigger_condition: Two graded runs still compose `.agents/skills/bmad-sdlc/../../../_bmad/scripts/...`; the symlink resolves into the authoring repo, and the guardrail forbids building a `..` path out of `{skill-root}`.
guard_snippet: Forbid any `..` path out of `{skill-root}` at the point of failure, and make step 1's in-place `customize.toml` fallback the only accepted response.
potential_consequence: The skill reads outside the project root and can pick up the authoring config; r12 R12-07 was meant to close this.
